text:
ashley: Heads-up — saw a clear p99 jump tied to cross-region fallback after yesterday's kernel selection pass. EU region had a spike when requests routed to us-west. Root looks like microbatch sizing + kernel change interaction. attaching profiler excerpt below.

tareq: Can you paste the p95/p99 deltas (regional + fallback hits)?

ashley: quick numbers from last hour:
```
EU primary (local kernels): p95=95ms p99=210ms
EU -> fallback (us-west): p95=160ms p99=1120ms
Overall EU p99 moved 210ms -> ~420ms after 00:15 UTC spike (percent fallback went from 0.8% -> 6.7%)
```
logs show KV cache miss amplification on fallback path (more full-attention kernel runs).

marta: ack. Do we know what microbatch sizing was in the canary? I thought we bumped target_microbatch to 16 to improve throughput.

ashley: yep — we changed target_microbatch=16 and kernel_hint=q4f16_opt_v2 on the canary nodes. On local EU nodes microbatching + kv-cache prefix helped, but when routed cross-region the extra network RTT made larger microbatches amplify tail latency because batching held requests waiting for slow remote shards.

kai: TL;DR: bigger microbatch -> higher aggregation latency; cross-region fallback multiplies that by RTT. That fits. Any profiling traces?

ashley: pasted a flame snippet (trimmed):
```
0. total 1120ms (fallback request)
 - network RTT 220ms
 - batch wait 340ms (waiting for batch fill)
 - kernel exec 420ms (q4f16_opt_v2)
 - kv-cache miss handling 130ms
```
On non-fallback local runs the batch wait is ~60ms and kernel exec 180-220ms.

tareq: two knobs: reduce target_microbatch for routes that may fallback, or change fallback policy to prefer same-region even under burst (until capacity threshold). Could also add a max-batch-wait-per-route limiter.

marta: suggestion: for immediate mitigation roll back target_microbatch to 8 for EU canary nodes and add routing hint to prefer eu-optimized kernel on fallback (if available). Also test a routing policy tweak: prefer latency over cost for eu customers.

kai: agree. Also consider kernel selection cost model update: prefer lower-latency kernels for routes where RTT > X ms. The scheduler currently picks kernels by throughput/cost estimate not by combined latency+RTT impact.

ashley: created a quick routing config we can try in dev: 
```
routing_policy:
  eu-region:
    preference: latency_preferred
    fallback_threshold: 0.05 # only fallback if >5% capacity saturation
batching:
  target_microbatch: 8
  max_batch_wait_ms: 80
kernel_hints:
  prefer_low_latency: true
```
I'll push this to the eu canary group if we agree.

perf-bot: scheduled perf run: canary_eu_microbatch8_1h -> 100k requests starting in 10m. Results will be posted here. :robot_face:

tareq: for longer term: add a microbatch-vs-RTT tradeoff simulation in the perf harness (synthesize RTT distributions and measure p95/p99 for routing mixes). We need automations that flag when throughput-optimizing knob increases p99 for >X customers.

marta: capturing that as action item. Also add a test for KV cache cold-miss amplification on fallback paths. If kv miss amplifies kernel exec by >1.5x when cross-region, we should bias routing away.

kai: small experiment idea: keep microbatch=16 but add per-request max-wait deadline that will force microbatch flush if head RTD > Yms. Might keep throughput while bounding tail.

ashley: all good — rolling the config to eu canary in 5m. Will post perf-bot output and a brief postmortem if this reduces p99. Thanks.

perf-bot: perf run complete. Summary:
```
canary_eu_microbatch8_1h (100k reqs):
 - overall p95=110ms p99=260ms
 - fallback p99 (eu->us) = 430ms (down from 1120ms)
 - throughput -6% vs microbatch16 canary
```

marta: looks like expected tradeoff: small throughput loss, big p99 win. I'll file a short RFC to update routing heuristics + kernel-selection cost model.

ashley: filing RFC -> will @tareq and @kai for review. Closing thread after RFC link posted. :white_check_mark:
